turns.content: Convert 0.100 g of Fe(OH)3 to moles using 106.9 g/mol.
Using the final volume and solid identity established above, derive the applicable solubility relation, insert Ksp=1.1e-36, and obtain the equilibrium pH.
Use that pH and the solution volume established above to calculate the residual moles of free H+.
From the dissolution equation and iron oxidation state established above, calculate the stoichiometric amount of acid consumed by the sample.
Add the stoichiometric demand and residual free H+ to obtain the total supplied acid.
Convert that amount to the minimum volume of 0.100 M monobasic strong acid and report it with the equilibrium pH.
